question.text: What is the role of FATF-Style Regional Bodies (FSRBs) in the global AML/CFT framework?

answer.text: FSRBs promote the adoption and implementation of FATF Recommendations within their respective regions and assist in conducting mutual evaluations of their member jurisdictions
FSRBs have the authority to directly prosecute money laundering cases in their member countries
FSRBs operate independently from FATF and set their own separate AML/CFT standards
FSRBs are limited to providing financial assistance to developing countries for AML programs

explanation.text: The Logic: Nine FSRBs form FATF's global network. FATF assists the SRBs to conduct mutual evaluations of their member jurisdictions, and the FATF 40 Recommendations serve as the principal AML/CFT standards used across that network. FSRBs therefore promote adoption and implementation of those standards regionally and support the mutual evaluation process. The Trap: Option C is the separate-standards distractor — FSRBs do not set their own separate AML/CFT standards. Option B is the direct-prosecution distractor — FSRBs have no power to prosecute money laundering cases in member jurisdictions. Note: India belongs to two FSRBs (APG and EAG) within the FATF network; mutual evaluations conducted under that network directly shape Indian regulatory expectations and IFSC compliance obligations.
